_comment: Per-app answers for the Questions section on apps/<id>.html (tools/gen-site-pages.js). Only `controls` is read today: one or two sentences on how the program is played, used verbatim as the answer to 'What are the controls?'. Ids without an entry get a generic answer. Keep these to what has been measured or read out of the program: the comments in lib/apps.js next to each touchControls block are the source for the games with on-screen pads.
snake: Arrow keys steer the snake and F2 starts a level. On a phone there is a four-way pad, swipes on the board also turn, and a New game button.
ski32: The skier follows the mouse pointer, so moving the mouse (or dragging on a phone) steers. F makes the skier go fast and F2 starts a new run; both are on-screen buttons on a phone.
pinball: Z is the left flipper, / is the right flipper, Space pulls the plunger, X and . nudge the table, and F2 starts a new game. On a phone the left half of the table flips left, the right half flips right, and the strip over the plunger lane launches the ball.
wep16_rodent: Arrow keys move the mouse one square and push the block in front of it, F2 deals a new game and F3 pauses. On a phone a four-way pad and swipes on the board move.
funtris: Left and Right move the brick, Up rotates, Down soft-drops, Space hard-drops, and F2 starts a new game. On a phone there is a four-way pad plus Drop and New game buttons.
winmine_wep: Left-click uncovers a square and right-click flags one. F2 starts a new game.
sol: Drag cards with the mouse. Double-click sends a card to its foundation. F2 deals a new game and the Game menu holds the scoring and draw options.
freecell: Click a card and then click where it should go, or drag it. F2 deals a new game; Ctrl+Z is not available, the original has no undo.
spider: Drag cards between columns and click the stock at the bottom right to deal a new row. F2 starts a new game and the Game menu sets the number of suits.
cruel: Drag cards onto a foundation or another column; the Game menu re-deals the columns, which is the game's one special move.
golf: Click a card in the columns that is one rank above or below the top of the stock pile; click the stock to turn the next card.
taipei: Click two matching free tiles to remove them. The Game menu offers a hint and a new layout.
reversi: Click a square to place a piece. The Game menu picks the difficulty.
pegged: Click a peg and then the hole two spaces away to jump; the Options menu chooses the board layout.
tictac: Click a cell on one of the boards to play. The Game menu chooses who goes first.
dxball: The mouse moves the paddle. Click to launch the ball, P pauses, and Escape opens the menu.
marbles: The mouse selects marbles and moves them. Choose a game from the opening menu.
mspaint98: The mouse draws with the selected tool; the palette at the bottom picks colours, the box on the left picks tools, and the menus hold image and zoom options.
notepad: Type in the window. The Edit menu has Find and Replace, the Search menu has Find Next (F3), and the Format menu sets the font and word wrap.
wordpad: Type in the window and use the toolbar or the Format menu for fonts and paragraphs. File > Open reads RTF and Word 6 documents from the virtual disk.
calc: Click the buttons or type: digits, + - * /, Enter for =, Escape to clear. The View menu switches to scientific mode.
winamp: Click Play or drag the position slider. The playlist and equalizer windows toggle from the buttons on the main window, and the volume slider is on the main window.
heroes2_demo: The mouse does everything: left-click to select and move, right-click and hold for information. The adventure map scrolls when the pointer touches an edge.
rct: The mouse does everything. Scroll the map by dragging with the right button, and the toolbar at the top opens rides, scenery and finances.
blobby_volley: The keyboard moves the blobs; the game's own options screen shows the keys for each player, and the opening menu picks a computer opponent.
_sound_comment: Per-app answer to 'Does sound work?'. Measured 2026-09-06 by a headless sweep (pe-imports + --trace-api on the audio APIs) and a read of lib/host-audio.js: the wave, DirectSound, MCI and MIDI paths all reach Web Audio; PlaySoundA only plays SND_RESOURCE sounds. Apps not listed get the generic wave/DirectSound sentence.

_sound.notepad: Notepad has no sound of its own; the original only beeps on an error, and that beep is played.
_sound.calc: Calculator has no sound of its own; the original only beeps on an error, and that beep is played.
_sound.mspaint98: Paint has no sound of its own; the original only beeps on an error, and that beep is played.
_sound.wordpad: WordPad has no sound of its own; the original only beeps on an error, and that beep is played.
_sound.regedit: Registry Editor has no sound of its own; the original only beeps on an error, and that beep is played.
_sound.taskman: Task Manager has no sound; the original plays none.
_sound.freecell: FreeCell has no sound; the original plays none.
_sound.sol: Solitaire has no sound; the original plays none.
_sound.cruel: Cruel has no sound; the original plays none.
_sound.golf: Golf has no sound; the original plays none.
_sound.pegged: Pegged has no sound; the original plays none.
_sound.snake: Rattler has no sound; the original plays none.
_sound.reversi: Reversi has no sound; the original plays none.
_sound.winmine_wep: Minesweeper has no sound; the original plays none.
_sound.spider: Spider has no sound; the original plays none.
_sound.taipei: Taipei has no sound apart from an error beep, which is played.
_sound.tictac: TicTactics has no sound apart from an error beep, which is played.
_sound.wep16_rodent: Rodent's Revenge has no sound apart from an error beep, which is played.
_sound.empipe: Yes. The music is MIDI, played by a General MIDI synthesizer built into the page, so it sounds like a 1990s software synth rather than a specific sound card. Browsers only allow audio after a click or a key press.
_sound.marbles: Yes. Sound effects go through DirectSound to the browser's Web Audio and the music is MIDI, played by a General MIDI synthesizer built into the page. Browsers only allow audio after a click or a key press.
_sound.heroes2_demo: The sound effects and MIDI music work: effects go to Web Audio and the music plays on a General MIDI synthesizer built into the page. The CD audio tracks of the full game are not available, as there is no game CD mounted.
_sound.bricks: Bricks starts with sound switched off; the speaker icon at the left of the board (marked S) turns it on, and the setting is kept in its INI file. Its 15 sound files are included here and play through PlaySound once sound is on.
_sound.cwordzap: Yes. Word Zap's two sounds are stored in the executable as resources and play through Web Audio. Browsers only allow audio after a click or a key press.
_sound.qblackjack: Yes. Blackjack's three sound clips are played from memory through Web Audio. Browsers only allow audio after a click or a key press.
_sound.blobby_volley: Yes. Blobby Volley's hit sound is played from memory through Web Audio. Browsers only allow audio after a click or a key press, so it starts with your first input.
_sound.winamp: Yes. Decoded audio goes through the wave-out API to the browser's Web Audio once a track is loaded. Browsers only allow audio after a click or a key press, so it starts with your first input.
